subject: Sprint slice reclaim + temporary autoscale exemption for Cobalt Health pilot
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-05T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint slice reclaim + temporary autoscale exemption for Cobalt Health pilot

Team —

Heads-up: Cobalt Health just confirmed an on-site demo for next Tuesday (4/13) and asked for a short, high-throughput window for model evaluation. They want a 48-hour dedicated slice with predictable latency for clinical document processing (batch + interactive).

Asking for two things:
1) Can we carve a temporary 48h sprint slice from the East GPU pool (p3-style) starting 4/12 00:00 UTC to 4/14 00:00 UTC? They need ~50 concurrent req/sec with 4k context.
2) We need an autoscale policy exemption so the slice doesn't get preempted by normal soft-eviction for sprint traffic and can burst to the reserved buffer without tripping priority eviction.

Constraints:
- This is a paid pilot (deal: COB-ENTERPRISE-2026-04) but contract still finalizing; legal will sign a modified MPA by EOD Monday.
- We should avoid permanent carveouts; this is a one-off demonstration window.
- Ops needs a runbook and fallback model (quantized variant) in case of thermal pressure.

Can infra and product align on:
- feasibility of the 48h carve + what exact GPU counts we should reserve,
- who signs the autoscale-exemption, and what metrics we gate it on,
- ops owner for the runbook and the fallback model to surface to the client.

I can host a quick sync 30m today if helpful.

Jonas
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint slice reclaim + temporary autoscale exemption for Cobalt Health pilot

Thanks Jonas —

Short answer: probably yes, with conditions. Quick notes from capacity/readout: 
- For 50 req/sec at 4k we should plan for ~6x A100-equivalent slots across the east pool (estimate: 6 nodes).
- We can carve a 48h sprint slice but we need a pre-authorized ops exemption window created in the scheduler to prevent soft-eviction. That requires product sign-off and a ticketed approval (JIRA-OPS-1427).
- Gate the exemption on: 1) strict start/end timestamps, 2) a 10% bucket reserved for emergency preemption, and 3) a fallback model (int8) pinned to the same policy.

I'll need: exact start/end UTC, a short justification paragraph for the approval ticket, and confirmation that legal will sign the MPA before the demo.

If you want, Marcus/Lauren and I can own the ops runbook. Marcus take the lead on sizing and on-call plan.

Kimmie
VP, Dedicated Capacity & Partnerships

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-05T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint slice reclaim + temporary autoscale exemption for Cobalt Health pilot

Adding sizing details —

Per our profiling: 4k context clinical extraction model (fp16) is ~0.9 tokens/ms on A100-ish. For 50 rps with an average 600-token response, peak p99 latency target 250ms: we should target 6 nodes (12 GPUs) to allow concurrency + buffer. If we use int8 quantized variant as fallback we can drop to 8 GPUs.

Operational asks:
- Create an exemption policy that: prevents scheduler preemption for the slice but allows manual eviction by ops on signaled thermal events.
- Attach a rate-limiter at the LB so a client-side bug can't flood the slice.

I'll draft the runbook and a minimal L7 guardrail (rate limits + token caps) and post it to the Drive.

Marcus
Sr. Infra Manager

Attachment: capacity-runbook-draft.md (outline)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-05T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint slice reclaim + temporary autoscale exemption for Cobalt Health pilot

Looping in commercial ops notes and the ask I promised to surface to Sales Ops: 

From sales-side: Cobalt will sign a short addendum (one-off demo fee) if we guarantee the demo window and provide an engineer for the session. They also asked for a short SLA for demo responsiveness (max 2 min to respond to issues during the demo).

Questions for Product/Capacity:
- Are we comfortable with a manual approval path from infra lead + product director for this single exemption? Or do we need legal sign-off first?
- Pricing team: recommend adding a $5k demo assurance fee to the addendum to offset risks.

I put the MPA v2 and the proposed addendum in the Drive (cobalt-pilot-mpa-v2.pdf).

Laura
Enterprise AE Manager

From: sara.murphy@cobalthealth.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cobalthealth.com
Date: 2026-04-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint slice reclaim + temporary autoscale exemption for Cobalt Health pilot

Hi Jonas + team —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Confirming: Cobalt accepts the 4/12 00:00 UTC start and the scope (48h). We'll sign the addendum and return a scanned copy by EOD 4/11. We appreciate the engineer support during the demo — could you confirm point-of-contact and a mobile number for the session?

One more ask: can you include a heatmap of expected latencies and a contact for urgent rollbacks in the runbook? Clinical stakeholders will want that in writing.

Best,
Sara Murphy
Director, AI Operations
Cobalt Health
